title: InPlaceMigrator._reinjectWithTopup small-principal top-up truncation reverts the migrateIn batch
description: Two compounding integer-truncation facets on the same root (gross-up arithmetic on a small principal). CODE-001: when the shortfall grosses up to topup == 0 (mulDiv floors, :276), depositFor(token, user, 0) hits require(amount > 0) and reverts the atomic batch; the if (credited < amt) predicate (:273) is misaligned with depositFor's >0 precondition, so control never reaches the finalCredited backstop (:288-292). CODE-004: for amt < 1000 raw units, amt/1000 == 0, so require(finalCredited >= amt - amt/1000) (:292) collapses to zero-tolerance exact-par; the gross-up rounds DOWN so finalCredited is a few wei short -> revert. The advertised 0.1% slack evaporates below amt = 1000 units. Distinct from KI#2 (which blesses silent reward dust round-DOWN; this is a REVERT on the migration path, not a silent loss in reward accounting).
impact: None to principal. Integer-truncation causes an atomic revert on small-principal (sub-1000-unit dust) migrateIn slices; no value moves. Implementation-quality / availability arithmetic defect on the migration path, not an owner action and not a theft path.
attackPath: CODE-001: a migrateIn slice carries a principal whose shortfall grosses up to topup == 0; depositFor(token, user, 0) reverts on require(amount > 0), reverting the atomic batch before the finalCredited backstop is reached.

CODE-004: a migrateIn slice carries amt < 1000 raw units; amt/1000 == 0 collapses require(finalCredited >= amt - amt/1000) to exact-par; the round-down gross-up leaves finalCredited a few wei short -> revert.
recommendation: Align the >0 / truncation predicates: handle topup == 0 (and credited >= amt) before calling depositFor so control reaches the finalCredited backstop. Use a tolerance floor for the par check that does not collapse below amt = 1000 units (e.g. an absolute-wei slack in addition to the 0.1% relative slack).
